messages.content: 你能給我盧浮宮博物館未來3個月的展覽資訊嗎？然後告訴我巴黎地區最好的意式和中式餐廳嗎？

function.name: restaurant_info
function.description: Get restaurant information for a specific area. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: Location for which to find restaurants.

food_type.description: Type of cuisine for which to find restaurants. Default is 'all' if not specified.

function.name: exhibition_info
function.description: Get exhibition information for a specific museum. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

museum_name.description: Name of the museum for which to find exhibitions.

month.description: Number of upcoming months for which to retrieve exhibition details. Default is 1 if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants two things:

1) Exhibition info for Louvre Museum (卢浮宫博物馆) for next 3 months.

2) Best Italian and Chinese restaurants in Paris region.

We have tool definitions:

restaurant_info(location:string, food_type?:"Italian"|...).

exhibition_info(museum_name:string, month?:number). The default month=1; we need 3 months so pass month=3.

So call both functions accordingly.

We'll first get exhibition info with museum_name="Louvre", month=3.

Then get restaurant info twice: location="Paris", food_type="Italian"; then again location="Paris", food_type="Chinese".

Return results as JSON array containing objects from each function calls. According to instruction: "When you do use a function, your response should contain only one single line with valid json." So after calling function(s), respond with JSON object or array. Since multiple calls needed, maybe combine into an array of responses. But instructions say when using a function, output only JSON on its own line. We can make separate lines per function call? It says "If you want to invoke more than one function, just keep sending them until you're done". That implies we send a request for each function separately. Each time we produce a JSON line. After all data retrieved, we provide explanation. However they also said "Your answer will always be a list of objects ... If no relevant result found return empty list." That's about search queries. For function calls, it's different.

Thus approach: First call exhibition_info. Then call restaurant_info twice. Provide outputs sequentially. Finally give summary text.

But the system might expect us to chain calls. We'll proceed stepwise.

First function call: exhibition_info({"museum_name":"卢浮宫","month":3}). Use English name? Provided param expects museum_name string. Let's use "卢浮宫" or "Louvre"? Probably "卢浮宫" works but safe to use "卢浮宫". I'll use "卢浮宫".

Second: restaurant_info({"location":"巴黎地区","food_type":"Italian"}). Third: same with Chinese.

Let's generate calls.
